Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated offering looks promising for our inference workloads. Before we move to procurement we need clarity on a couple of contract items in the RFP (attached). Could you clarify: 1) how you define a "capacity unit" for Reserved capacity (is it GPU-hour, vGPU-equivalent, or a performance-equivalent unit?), 2) how throughput guarantees are measured (requests/sec vs tokens/sec vs model-specific baselines), and 3) the formula for service credits when SLA targets are missed.

On pricing side: Sienna is trying to map committed units to our internal cost buckets. We also need the discount schedule for incremental commits (e.g., 1x, 2x, 4x commitments over 12 months).

Attached is our procurement spreadsheet and the relevant RFP excerpt. Can you and your team propose precise contract language we can run through our legal team? Specifically we want unambiguous definitions so there isn't scope creep around burst capacity and autoscaling.

Thanks,

Sr. Procurement Manager
Sienna Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Hi Emma — great questions, and thanks for the RFP. I put together concise answers below and attached a draft SLA appendix (Draft_SLA_AppB_v2.docx) that maps the language to the contract. High level: we define capacity in performance-equivalent units and measure throughput at the token/sec level for generative workloads and requests/sec for short RPC-style calls.

1) Capacity unit definition (draft language):
- "Reserved Capacity Unit (RCU)": one RCU represents the baseline throughput of a single A10-equivalent device configured with model X benchmarks (baseline: 10k tokens/min for a 2k context generative model). Customers can convert other hardware equivalences using the published equivalence table (Section 1.2).

2) Throughput guarantees and measurement:
- Guarantees expressed as "Committed Throughput" (CT), measured in tokens/sec (for generation) or requests/sec (for non-generative endpoints). CT = RCUs * BaselineThroughputPerRCU. Measurement window is rolling 30 days, sampled at 5-minute intervals, with probes run from the customer-designated region.

3) Service credits (draft):
- If CT availability drops below the SLA target in a 30-day window, service credits are applied to the monthly invoice per the table in Appendix B (examples: <99.5% = 10% credit; <98% = 25% credit; repeated breaches capped at 50%). Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (>=48h notice), customer-induced overload/misconfiguration, force majeure.

Bursting & autoscaling: RCUs are reserved baseline. Bursts above CT are allowed on a best-effort basis and billed at overage rates (or drawn from pre-authorized burst pool), but must not be counted toward CT unless explicitly contracted.

I'll loop in Neha (sales) and Dev (legal) to propose a clean set of redlines we can deliver. If Sienna prefers different baselines (e.g., measure in requests/sec for your low-latency endpoints), we can publish an endpoint-specific baseline in the SLA appendix.

Attached: Draft_SLA_AppB_v2.docx — contains suggested redline snippets you can drop into your procurement doc.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Team — I reviewed Draft_SLA_AppB_v2 and Sienna's ask. Suggested redlines / final language below (high-level). I recommend we offer the 25% repeated-breach cap (concession) if we get stronger observability and a 60-day remediation pathway. Key points: 

- Terminology: replace any loose "capacity unit" language with "Reserved Capacity Unit (RCU)" and include a cross-reference table in Appendix B mapping common GPU SKUs to RCUs.

- Measurement: define the precise probe and aggregation algorithm: sample at 5-minute intervals, each sample returns tokens/sec and 95th-percentile latency per endpoint; CT availability = percentage of samples in the rolling 30-day window meeting CT thresholds. Define tie-breakers for transient network noise and require at least a 72-hour arbitration window before crediting.

- Remedies & caps: service credit table remains but cap repeated-breach exposure to 25% of monthly fees (company accepts this concession). Credits calculated as percentage of monthly Dedicated invoice for the impacted region and model family.

- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (>=48h notice), customer misconfiguration, abuse, third-party cloud outages outside Redwood control.

- Termination & Cure: remove immediate termination for single-month misses. Instead: (a) customer must notify Redwood with claim and logs; (b) Redwood has 30 days to propose mitigations; (c) if issues persist for 3 consecutive months despite remediation, customer may elect termination for convenience with 60 days' notice and prorated refund for unused prepaid RCUs.

- Auditability: Redwood will provide probe logs and calculation artifacts on request within 5 business days, with redactions for internal telemetry. For repeated disputes, offer a neutral third-party metric review for escalations.

I'll attach a redlined App B (internal) for Marcus to send to Sienna if approved. We should confirm pricing math with Finance but the concessions above are within acceptable risk if we secure a 12 or 24-month commit.

Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
